When solving an exercise at the end of [Chapter 18](../chapters/ch18-fft-wildcard-involution-matching.qmd) or [Chapter 20](../chapters/ch20-structural-isomorphism-weighted-strings.qmd), the chapter header immediately tells you whether to set up a polynomial cross-correlation over $\mathbb{F}_{998244353}$ or a window-clipped KMP failure table. In a live contest, **problems arrive completely untagged**. You are handed a specification about corrupted transmissions, relative trend matching, or exponentially long string macros, together with numerical constraints ($N \le 5 \times 10^5$, $k \le 2500$, or $|T| \le 10^{18}$), and you must diagnose which algebraic, Kangaroo, structural-isomorphism, or grammar-compression invariant governs the task.

This checkpoint tests **blind diagnostic recognition** across all four chapters of Part V (`Ch 18`–`Ch 21`). None of the visible problem titles or statements in Section 2 reveal which chapter or technique applies.

::: {.callout-important title="Zero-Spoiler Protocol & Progressive Hints"}

1. **Strict Zero-Spoiler Rule in Visible Statements**: Every problem statement (`CP-V-01` through `CP-V-07`) is written in pure contest form without naming the target chapter (`Ch 18`–`Ch 21`) or technique (`FFT Wildcard`, `Involution Matching`, `Kangaroo LCE`, `Order-Preserving KMP`, `Cartesian-Tree KMP`, `Locally Consistent Parsing`, `SLP`, `String Attractor`).
2. **Diagnose Before Peeking**: Before opening any dropdown on a problem, write down on scratch paper:
   - Which **Part V paradigm** (`Ch 18`–`Ch 21`) is triggered by the compatibility relation, error budget, and length scale;
   - Which **lookalike decoy paradigm** must be ruled out, and why;
   - The **combinatorial word or algebraic invariant** that collapses the naive $\Theta(NM)$ or $\Theta(|T|)$ bottleneck.
3. **Four-Stage Progressive Unmasking**:
   - **Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination**: Explains how to identify the governing paradigm and eliminate lookalike decoys purely from constraints and query semantics.
   - **Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant**: States the exact polynomial penalty, window-clipping identity, or seam-contraction invariant needed for the reduction.
   - **Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly**: Outlines the transform setup, failure-link predicate, or parse-tree traversal and its complexity target.
   - **Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution**: Full proof, boundary pitfall audit (`BP-5-01` through `BP-5-08`), and non-standard reference kernel where clarifying.
:::

## 1. Blind Diagnostic Triage Guide & Decoy Elimination

The most expensive tactical mistake in Part V contest problems is **confusing non-transitive algebraic compatibility with transitive structural isomorphism**, or **confusing approximate matching with grammar-compressed indexing**. Before tackling the seven blind problems below, study the two primary Part V **Diagnostic Decoy Comparisons** and the routing flowchart.

### 1.1 Decoy Triad A: Polynomial/Involution Matching (`Ch 18`) vs. Window-Clipped Structural KMP (`Ch 20`)

Both paradigms generalize exact character equality $P[j] = T[i+j]$ to a broader compatibility rule across all alignments $i \in [0, N-M]$. Why does KMP solve some of these in deterministic $O(N+M)$ time while failing catastrophically on others?

| Diagnostic Dimension | `Ch 18` Non-Transitive Polynomial FFT (`T-3B-01`, `T-3B-02`) | `Ch 18` Involution Exception ($\pi^2 = \mathrm{id}$ in `T-3B-02`) | `Ch 20` Window-Clipped Structural KMP (`T-3B-04`, `T-5B-06`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Governing Compatibility Relation** | **Non-transitive point-wise relation** $R(P_j, T_{i+j})$: wildcards `'?'`, distance $|a-b| \le k$, general permutation $T_{i+j} \in \{P_j, \pi(P_j)\}$ ($\pi^2 \ne \mathrm{id}$), or affine $T = \alpha P + \beta$. | **Symmetric 2-cycle compatibility**: $T_{i+j} \in \{P_j, \pi(P_j)\}$ where $\pi(\pi(c)) = c$ for every $c \in \Sigma$. | **Context-relative substring equivalence** $U \cong V$: bijective renaming (`p-KMP`), relative rank (`Order-KMP`), or min-heap topology (`Cartesian-KMP`). |
| **Is Substring Equivalence Transitive?** | **No**: $\texttt{a} \approx \texttt{?}$ and $\texttt{?} \approx \texttt{b}$, yet $\texttt{a} \not\approx \texttt{b}$. Border transitivity collapses completely. | **Yes**: $\Sigma$ partitions into disjoint 2-cycles $\{c, \pi(c)\}$ and fixed points; canonicalizing each 2-cycle to $\min(c, \pi(c))$ restores exact equality! | **Yes (after window clipping!)**: $U \cong V$ and $V \cong W \implies U \cong W$, and restricting to a suffix preserves equivalence once backward offsets $> q$ are clipped to $0$. |
| **Optimal Engine & Time Complexity** | **Index-Reflection FFT / NTT** ($P^R[M-1-j]$) in $O(N \log N)$ (1-NTT Indicator, 2-NTT Kalai, or $\sqrt{M\log M}$ value buckets). | **Canonicalized Exact KMP** in deterministic **$O(N + M)$ time with zero FFTs**! | **Window-Clipped KMP** (`clip(v, q) = v <= q ? v : 0` or `LMax`/`LMin`) in **$O(N + M)$** (or $O(N + M\log M)$). |
| **Fatal Misdiagnosis** | Running KMP on wildcards or general $\pi$, OR forgetting harmonic multiple sieving `bad[d] \|= conflict[k*d]` when a *single* wildcard string must have period $d$. | Paying 3 NTTs or complex FFT precision risk when the given cipher satisfies $\pi(\pi(c)) = c$. | Comparing unclipped `prev_T[i]` against `prev_P[q+1]`, or caching `clip(prev_T[i], q)` outside the KMP `while (q > 0)` loop! |

### 1.2 Decoy Pair B: $k$-Mismatch Period Dichotomy (`Ch 19`) vs. Locally Consistent Parsing & Compressed Indexing (`Ch 21`)

Both paradigms rely on **LCE (Longest Common Extension) queries** and **Run-Length / Periodic Compression** to bypass character-by-character scanning. How do you distinguish their operating regimes?

| Diagnostic Dimension | `Ch 19` $k$-Mismatch & $2k$-Period Dichotomy (`T-3B-03`) | `Ch 21` Locally Consistent Parsing, SLPs & Attractors (`T-3B-05`, `T-5B-05`, `T-5B-08`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Problem Symptom** | Explicit strings $P, T$ ($N, M \le 5 \times 10^5$) with an **error budget** of $\le k$ Hamming mismatches or $\le k$ Levenshtein edits ($k \ge 1$). | **Exact** matching, LCE, cut/paste, or factor counting on **exponentially long strings** ($N \le 10^{18}$), dynamic text edits, or $z$-phrase LZ77 / SLP grammars. |
| **Role of LCE & RLE** | **Kangaroo Jumps** skip $\le k+1$ exact segments in $O(1)$ per jump; when $\operatorname{per}(P) = p \le 2k$, $P$ and $T$ compress into **$\le 3k$ RLE runs modulo $p$** for $O(N\sqrt{k\log k})$ convolution. | **Alternating Contraction (`RComp` + `PComp`)** shrinks string length by $\le 5/6$ per level with $O(1)$ local lookahead radius $\Delta$, giving $O(\log N)$ deterministic LCE and $O(1)$ seam modifications per level. |
| **Primary Boundary / Seam Invariant** | **Clamping**: $\ell = \min(\operatorname{LCE}(j, i+j-1), M-j+1)$ prevents jumping past $M$; **Diagonal Wavefront**: $L_{e, d}$ transitions from $d, d-1, d+1$. | **Primary-Seam Non-Proliferation**: every factor crosses a unique split $X_u \to X_L X_R$; **RLE Early Termination**: at $\operatorname{Run}(c, \ell_1)$ vs. $\operatorname{Run}(c, \ell_2)$ with $\ell_1 \ne \ell_2$, return $+\min(\ell_1, \ell_2)$ and **stop immediately**! |
| **Fatal Misdiagnosis** | Running $O(Nk)$ Kangaroo jumps when $k = 3000$, or running $|\Sigma|$ FFTs when $|\Sigma| = 10^5$ (must use Abrahamson $\sqrt{M\log M}$ or $2k$-Period Dichotomy). | Using a standard randomized treap for $N \le 10^{18}$ (tree splits depend on global index, desynchronizing equal substrings at different shifts!), or forgetting to strip $O(\Delta)$ margin symbols when compressing a query pattern $P$. |

## 2. Unspoiled Blind Checkpoint Problems (`CP-V-01` – `CP-V-07`)

---

### Problem `CP-V-01` — Minimum Alphabet-Coalescing Distance

You are given a text string $T[0..N-1]$ and a pattern string $P[0..M-1]$ ($1 \le M \le N \le 1.25 \times 10^5$), both consisting only of the first six lowercase English letters $\Sigma = \{\texttt{a}, \texttt{b}, \texttt{c}, \texttt{d}, \texttt{e}, \texttt{f}\}$.

In a single **coalescing operation** applied simultaneously to a substring $U = T[i..i+M-1]$ and $P[0..M-1]$, you may choose any two letters $x, y \in \Sigma$ and replace every occurrence of $x$ in both $U$ and $P$ with $y$. For each starting alignment $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, N - M\}$, compute the **minimum number of coalescing operations** required to make $T[i..i+M-1]$ identical to $P[0..M-1]$.

- **Constraints**: $1 \le M \le N \le 1.25 \times 10^5$, $|\Sigma| = 6$, Time Limit $4.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination (`Ch 18` vs. `Ch 20` Decoy Triad)**: At first sight, renaming characters to make $T[i..i+M-1]$ match $P$ sounds like `Ch 20` Parameterized Matching (`p-KMP`). **Why does `p-KMP` fail here?** Because `p-KMP` tests for a *bijection* (zero coalescing operations, where distinct characters stay distinct), whereas here we are allowed to **merge** distinct characters into a single equivalence class! Merging characters is a many-to-one quotient map governed by connected components on $\Sigma$.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: At alignment $i$, position $j \in [0, M-1]$ demands that character $P[j]$ and character $T[i+j]$ be merged into the same equivalence class. Viewing $\Sigma$ as a $6$-vertex undirected graph $G_i = (\Sigma, E_i)$ where edge $\{a, b\} \in E_i$ exists iff there is at least one $j \in [0, M-1]$ with $\{P[j], T[i+j]\} = \{a, b\}$, the minimum number of coalescing operations at shift $i$ is simply:
  $$\sum_{\text{component } C \text{ of } G_i} (|C| - 1) = |\Sigma| - \operatorname{cc}(G_i) = 6 - \operatorname{cc}(G_i).$$
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
How do we determine for all $i \in [0, N-M]$ and all ordered pairs $(a, b) \in \Sigma \times \Sigma$ ($a \ne b$) whether there exists $j \in [0, M-1]$ with $P[j] = a$ and $T[i+j] = b$?
Define binary indicator polynomials using **Index-Reflection Duality (`Ch 18` Lemma 18.1)**:
$$A_a(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{M-1} \mathbf{1}[P[M-1-k] = a]\, x^k, \qquad B_b(x) = \sum_{t=0}^{N-1} \mathbf{1}[T[t] = b]\, x^t.$$
Then the coefficient $[x^{i + M - 1}]\bigl(A_a(x) B_b(x)\bigr) = \sum_{j=0}^{M-1} \mathbf{1}[P[j] = a]\, \mathbf{1}[T[i+j] = b]$ counts the exact number of positions $j$ aligning $a$ in $P$ with $b$ in $T$. Thus undirected edge $\{a, b\}$ is present in $G_i$ if and only if:
$$[x^{i + M - 1}]\Bigl(A_a(x) B_b(x) + A_b(x) B_a(x)\Bigr) > 0.$$
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. Choose FFT length $L = 2^{\lceil \log_2(N + M - 1) \rceil} \le 2^{18} = 262144$.
2. **Pre-transform Caching**: Instead of running an FFT inside the pair loop $(a, b)$, compute the **6 forward DFTs** $\widehat{A}_a = \operatorname{DFT}_L(A_a)$ and **6 forward DFTs** $\widehat{B}_b = \operatorname{DFT}_L(B_b)$ **once** (only $12$ forward transforms total, or $6$ via 2-in-1 complex packing!).
3. For each of the $\binom{6}{2} = 15$ unordered pairs $\{a, b\}$ ($0 \le a < b < 6$):
   - Pointwise compute $\widehat{C}_{a,b}[k] = \widehat{A}_a[k]\widehat{B}_b[k] + \widehat{A}_b[k]\widehat{B}_a[k]$ for $k \in [0, L-1]$.
   - Run 1 inverse transform $C_{a,b} = \operatorname{IDFT}_L(\widehat{C}_{a,b})$ (or pack pairs of $C_{a,b}$ into 8 complex IFFTs).
   - For each shift $i \in [0, N-M]$, if $\lfloor C_{a,b}[i + M - 1] + 0.5 \rfloor > 0$, union $a$ and $b$ in a 6-element Disjoint Set Union (DSU) for shift $i$.
4. Output $6 - \operatorname{cc}(G_i)$ for each $i \in [0, N-M]$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-V-01"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 18](../chapters/ch18-fft-wildcard-involution-matching.qmd) (`T-3B-01`: Index-Reflection Cross-Correlation, Frequency-Domain Reuse & Dual-Real Complex FFT Packing; `CF 954I — Yet Another String Matching Problem`)**.
- **Why Naive Pairwise Convolution TLEs & How Frequency Reuse Cuts Transforms by $3.4\times$**:
  There are $6 \times 5 = 30$ ordered pairs $(a, b)$ with $a \ne b$. A naive loop calling `multiply(A_a, B_b)` 30 times executes $30 \times 3 = 90$ FFTs of length $2^{18}$. By computing $\widehat{A}_0, \dots, \widehat{A}_5$ and $\widehat{B}_0, \dots, \widehat{B}_5$ up front ($12$ transforms) and combining $\widehat{A}_a \odot \widehat{B}_b + \widehat{A}_b \odot \widehat{B}_a$ in the frequency domain before inverting for each of the $\binom{6}{2} = 15$ undirected edges ($15$ inverse transforms), the total transform count drops from $90$ to $27$ (and to $6 + 8 = 14$ complex FFTs with conjugate packing!).

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-5-01`)**:
  - **Re-running Forward DFTs Inside the $(a, b)$ Loop**: Causes immediate Time Limit Exceeded. Always cache the $|\Sigma|$ forward DFTs whenever pairwise alphabet cross-correlations are needed.
- **Complexity**: $O\bigl((|\Sigma| + \binom{|\Sigma|}{2}) N \log N + |\Sigma|^2 N \alpha(|\Sigma|)\bigr)$ time and $O(|\Sigma| N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-V-02` — Dual-Mode Telemetry Frame Repair

A satellite telemetry frame $S[0..N-1]$ ($2 \le N \le 5 \times 10^5$) is transmitted over a 26-letter alphabet $\Sigma = \{\texttt{a}, \dots, \texttt{z}\}$ together with erasure markers `'?'`. You are also given a hardware cipher permutation $\tau: \Sigma \to \Sigma$ that is **self-inverse** ($\tau(\tau(c)) = c$ for every $c \in \Sigma$). Each `'?'` in $S$ represents a lost character that can be replaced by any letter in $\Sigma$.

You must analyze the self-overlap structure of $S$ under two distinct engineering specifications:

1. **Mode A (Two-Copy Paired-Cipher Border Check)**: Suppose two *independent* receivers receive copies of $S$ and fill in their `'?'` erasures independently to produce concrete strings $S_1, S_2 \in \Sigma^N$. Find all proper border lengths $b \in \{1, 2, \dots, N-1\}$ for which there exist repairs $S_1, S_2$ satisfying $S_1[k] = \tau(S_2[N - b + k])$ for all $0 \le k < b$.
2. **Mode B (Single-Copy Consistent Period & Border Check, $\tau = \mathrm{id}$)**: Now suppose $\tau$ is the identity ($\tau(c) = c$) and a **single** repaired string $S^* \in \Sigma^N$ must be formed by filling each `'?'` in $S$ once. Find all proper border lengths $b \in \{1, 2, \dots, N-1\}$ for which there exists a single consistent repair $S^*$ satisfying $S^*[0..b-1] = S^*[N-b..N-1]$.

- **Constraints**: $2 \le N \le 5 \times 10^5$, $\tau(\tau(c)) = c$, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination**: Why do Mode A and Mode B produce **different** answers whenever $b > N / 2$?
  - In **Mode A**, the prefix $S_1[0..b-1]$ and suffix $S_2[N-b..N-1]$ come from two *independent* repairs of $S$. Even when $b > N/2$ (so index $k \in [N-b, b-1]$ lies in both the prefix and the suffix), $S_1[k]$ and $S_2[k]$ are chosen independently! Thus $b$ is valid in Mode A iff shift $d = N - b$ has no direct conflict between $S[k]$ and $S[k + d]$.
  - In **Mode B**, there is only **one** string $S^*$. If $b > N/2$ and $S[d] = \texttt{?}$, then $S^*[d]$ must simultaneously equal $S^*[0]$ (from $k = 0$) and $S^*[2d]$ (from $k = d$). By Period–Border Duality (`Ch 01`), $S^*$ has border $b$ iff $S^*$ has period $d = N - b$, which holds iff every residue class modulo $d$ contains at most one distinct concrete letter—i.e., **no multiple $m = c \cdot d < N$** has a direct conflict $S[k] \ne S[k + m]$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}

1. **Handling the Involution $\tau$ Without Increasing Polynomial Degree**:
   In Mode A, we require $S_1[k] = \tau(S_2[k + d])$ whenever both $S[k]$ and $S[k + d]$ are non-`'?'`. Define the $\tau$-transformed copy $T[j] = \tau(S[j])$ (with $\tau(\texttt{?}) = \texttt{?}$). Then the condition $S_1[k] = \tau(S_2[k+d])$ between $S$ and $S$ is **100% equivalent** to standard wildcard compatibility $S[k] \approx T[k + d]$ between $S$ and $T$!
   *(Even better: if there were no wildcards and the rule were $T[i+j] \in \{P[j], \tau(P[j])\}$ as in `CF 1334G` with $\tau^2 = \mathrm{id}$, collapsing each 2-cycle $\{c, \tau(c)\}$ to $\min(c, \tau(c))$ solves it via $O(N)$ KMP with zero FFTs!)*

2. **Single-Prime Collision-Free Degree-Reduced Indicator NTT (`Ch 18` `T-3B-01`)**:
   Map `'?'` to $(u_x, v_x) = (0, 0)$ and each letter $c \in \Sigma$ to $(1, \operatorname{ord}(c) \in \{1, \dots, 26\})$. For shift $d \in [1, N-1]$, the discrepancy between $S[0..N-1-d]$ and $T[d..N-1]$ is:
   $$D_{\mathrm{ind}}(d) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1-d} u_{S[k]}\, u_{T[k+d]}\, \bigl(v_{S[k]} - v_{T[k+d]}\bigr)^2.$$
   Because $0 \le D_{\mathrm{ind}}(d) \le N (|\Sigma| - 1)^2 = 5 \times 10^5 \times 625 = 3.125 \times 10^8 < 998244353$, **a single NTT prime $Q = 998244353$ has zero modular wrap-around and zero false positives!**
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. **Mode A**: Build $T[j] = (S[j] == \texttt{?} \text{ ? } \texttt{?} : \tau(S[j]))$. Reverse $S$ to $S^R[k] = S[N-1-k]$ and evaluate:
   $$D_{\mathrm{ind}}(d) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1-d} (u_{S[k]} v_{S[k]}^2)\, u_{T[k+d]} - 2 \sum_{k=0}^{N-1-d} (u_{S[k]} v_{S[k]})\, (u_{T[k+d]} v_{T[k+d]}) + \sum_{k=0}^{N-1-d} u_{S[k]}\, (u_{T[k+d]} v_{T[k+d]}^2)$$
   at convolution index $(N - 1 - k) + (k + d) = N - 1 + d$ using 3 NTT forward pairs + 1 accumulated INTT modulo $998244353$. Border $b = N - d$ is valid in Mode A iff $D_{\mathrm{ind}}(d) = 0$.

2. **Mode B ($\tau = \mathrm{id}$, so $T = S$)**: Using the conflict array `conflict[m] = (D_ind(m) > 0)` for $m \in [1, N-1]$, run a harmonic sieve over all multiples of $d = N - b$:
   ```cpp
   for (int d = 1; d < N; ++d)
       for (int m = d; m < N; m += d)
           if (conflict[m]) { bad_period[d] = true; break; }
   ```
   Border $b$ is valid in Mode B iff `!bad_period[N - b]`.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-V-02"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 18](../chapters/ch18-fft-wildcard-involution-matching.qmd) (`T-3B-01` & `T-3B-02`: Degree-Reduced Indicator 1-NTT Wildcards, Involution Reduction & Harmonic Period Sieve; Generalized Matching Decoy · Part 1)**.
- **Concrete Counterexample Separating Mode A and Mode B**:
  Let $S = \texttt{a?b}$ ($N = 3$) with $\tau = \mathrm{id}$, and test border length $b = 2$ (shift $d = N - b = 1$):

  - **Mode A (Two Independent Copies)**: Set $S_1 = \texttt{abb}$ and $S_2 = \texttt{aab}$. Then prefix $S_1[0..1] = \texttt{ab}$ equals suffix $S_2[1..2] = \texttt{ab}$! Indeed, at shift $d = 1$, $(S[0], S[1]) = (\texttt{a}, \texttt{?})$ and $(S[1], S[2]) = (\texttt{?}, \texttt{b})$ have $D_{\mathrm{ind}}(1) = 0$.
  - **Mode B (Single Consistent Fill $S^*$)**: Any single string $S^* = \texttt{a} c \texttt{b}$ having border $b = 2$ must satisfy $S^*[0] = S^*[1] \implies c = \texttt{a}$ and $S^*[1] = S^*[2] \implies c = \texttt{b}$, a contradiction! The conflict is detected at the multiple $m = 2d = 2$, where $(S[0], S[2]) = (\texttt{a}, \texttt{b})$ has $D_{\mathrm{ind}}(2) > 0$.
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-5-02`, `BP-5-03`)**:
  - **Mapping `'a'..'z'` to `0..25` or Raw ASCII `97..122` (`BP-5-02`)**: If `'a'` is mapped to $0$, `'a'` acts as a wildcard! If raw cubic weights $v^3 T$ are used without boolean outer indicators $u_S u_T$, then $N \cdot 26^4 \approx 2.28 \times 10^{11} > 998244353$ can wrap around to $0 \pmod{998244353}$. Always use $(u, v) \in \{0\} \times \{0\} \cup \{1\} \times \{1..|\Sigma|\}$.
  - **Omitting the Harmonic Multiple Loop in Mode B (`BP-5-03`)**: Fails on `a?b` at $d = 1$.
- **Complexity**: $O(N \log N)$ time and $O(N)$ space for both modes.
::::

### Problem `CP-V-03` — Fault-Tolerant Cipher Alignment

You are given a long intercepted message $T[1..N]$ and a template message $P[1..M]$ ($1 \le M \le N \le 10^5$) over an integer alphabet $\Sigma = \{1, 2, \dots, 10^5\}$, together with a fault tolerance $k$ ($0 \le k \le 5$).

A contiguous window $W = T[i..i+M-1]$ is a **$k$-fault substitution match** of $P[1..M]$ if you can change the values of **at most $k$ positions** in $W$ to produce a modified window $W'[1..M]$ that is **bijectively isomorphic** to $P[1..M]$—that is, there exists a bijection $\pi: \Sigma \to \Sigma$ such that $\pi(W'[j]) = P[j]$ for all $1 \le j \le M$. Find all valid starting alignments $i \in \{1, 2, \dots, N - M + 1\}$.

- **Constraints**: $1 \le M \le N \le 10^5$, $|\Sigma| \le 10^5$, $0 \le k \le 5$, Time Limit $2.5\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination (`Ch 19` + `Ch 20` Synthesis vs. `Ch 18`)**:
  - If $k = 0$, this is pure Parameterized Pattern Matching (`Ch 20`), solvable in $O(N + M)$ time via window-clipped `p-KMP`.
  - However, when $k \ge 1$ character corruptions are allowed, `p-KMP`'s prefix-border automaton breaks because a single corrupted character alters the backward-offset encoding of the string. Conversely, $|\Sigma| \le 10^5$ and bijective renaming rule out `Ch 18` FFT indicator convolutions.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Combine **`Ch 20`'s Window-Clipped Backward Offset Encoding (`prev` array)** with **`Ch 19`'s Landau–Vishkin Kangaroo LCE Jumps**! Specifically, how many entries of the window-clipped `prev` array can change when we modify **one** character $W[j]$?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Recall from `Ch 20` that two strings $A[1..M]$ and $B[1..M]$ are bijectively isomorphic iff their window-clipped backward-offset arrays $\operatorname{prev}_A[1..M]$ and $\operatorname{prev}_B[1..M]$ are identical, where $\operatorname{prev}_A[j] = j - \max\{r < j : A[r] = A[j]\}$ ($0$ if none).

> **The $2$-Jump Mutation Bound under Single-Character Substitution**:
> Suppose we change a single position $W[j]$ from old symbol $x$ to new symbol $y$. Which indices $r \in [1, M]$ can change their backward offset $\operatorname{prev}_W[r]$?
>
> 1. Position $r = j$ itself (whose predecessor changes from the last $x$ before $j$ to the last $y$ before $j$);
> 2. At most **one** later position $r_x > j$: the *first* occurrence of $x$ after $j$ (whose predecessor used to be $j$, and now skips back to the previous $x$ before $j$);
> 3. At most **one** later position $r_y > j$: the *first* occurrence of $y$ after $j$ (whose predecessor now becomes $j$).
>
> Conversely, scanning left-to-right from $j = 1$ to $M$ via Kangaroo jumps on the `prev` arrays (`p-LCE`), the **very first** index $j$ where $\operatorname{clip}(\operatorname{prev}_T[i+j-1], j-1) \ne \operatorname{prev}_P[j]$ pinpoints a conflict between $T[i+j-1]$ and the unique earlier position $j - \operatorname{prev}_P[j]$ (or $\operatorname{prev}_T$), leaving at most $2$ candidate character reassignments to branch on (or at most $2k$ `p-LCE` jumps to verify a candidate bijection)!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. **Fast `p-LCE` Oracle (`Ch 20` §1.3 / Theorem 20.2 Baker's Single-Position Mutation)**:
   Build a **Persistent Segment Tree of polynomial rolling hashes** over the dynamic `prev` arrays of suffixes $T[i..N]$ (scanning $i$ from $N$ down to $1$: advancing $i+1 \to i$ only mutates position $\operatorname{next}_T[i]$ from $0$ to $\operatorname{next}_T[i] - i$!) and similarly for $P$. This supports `p-LCE(P[j..], T[i+j-1..])` (relative to window start $1$ and $i$) or static-array LCE between modified breakpoints in $O(\log M)$ time!

2. **Bounded-Branching / Kangaroo Verification at Shift $i$**:
   - Actually, even simpler than branching on character values: when scanning $j = 1 \dots M$ at shift $i$, maintain a small set of at most $k$ **overridden positions** (or at most $k$ pinned character pairs $(c_P, c_T)$ that were forced by earlier mismatches, modifying at most $2k$ dynamic breakpoints in the `prev` array of $T[i..i+M-1]$!).
   - Between the $\le 2k$ dynamic breakpoints where a corrupted position $q < j$ alters $\operatorname{prev}_T[r]$ ($r = \operatorname{next}_T[q]$), the `prev` array of $T[i..i+M-1]$ is unmodified, so we leap across exact-matching segments using `p-LCE` in $O(\log M)$ time per jump!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-V-03"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 19](../chapters/ch19-kmismatch-wavefront-period-dichotomy.qmd) & [Chapter 20](../chapters/ch20-structural-isomorphism-weighted-strings.qmd) (`T-3B-03` + `T-3B-04`: Kangaroo LCE Jumps Coupled with Window-Clipped Parameterized Offsets; Generalized Matching Decoy · Part 2)**.
- **Exact Conflict Resolution at the First `prev` Mismatch**:
  Suppose $W[1..j-1]$ (after $\le e$ edits) is already parameterized-isomorphic to $P[1..j-1]$ via a partial bijection $\pi$, and `p-LCE` stops at index $j$ where the clipped backward offset of $W[j]$ disagrees with $\operatorname{prev}_P[j]$:

  - **Case 1 ($\operatorname{prev}_P[j] > 0$)**: $P[j]$ is a repeat of $P[j_0]$ where $j_0 = j - \operatorname{prev}_P[j] < j$. Thus in any valid continuation that does not edit $j_0$, the character at $W[j]$ is **uniquely forced** to equal $W[j_0]$! We can either (Branch A) pay $1$ edit to change $W[j] \leftarrow W[j_0]$, or (Branch B, only if $j_0$ was the * very first* occurrence of $P[j_0]$!) pay $1$ edit to change $W[j_0] \leftarrow W[j]$.
  - **Case 2 ($\operatorname{prev}_P[j] = 0$, so $\operatorname{clip}(\operatorname{prev}_W[j], j-1) = d > 0$)**: $P[j]$ is a brand-new symbol, whereas $W[j]$ repeats $W[j - d]$. We either edit $W[j]$ to a fresh unused symbol, or (if $j - d$ was a first occurrence) edit $W[j - d]$.
  In fact, if we simply ask whether $\operatorname{Ham}(\pi(W), P) \le k$, note that any character $c$ occurring $\ge k + 1$ times in $P$ has its partner $\pi^{-1}(c)$ uniquely determined by majority vote, while positions where $W[j]$ is edited to match $\pi^{-1}(P[j])$ are found by jumping to the next `p-LCE` discrepancy and deleting/ignoring the conflicting position $j$ (or $j_0$) from the predecessor chain!

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-5-04`)**:
  - **Assuming 1 Character Substitution Causes Only 1 `prev`-Array Mismatch**: Consider $P = \texttt{aba}$ ($\operatorname{prev}_P = [0, 0, 2]$) and $W = \texttt{aaa}$ ($\operatorname{prev}_W = [0, 1, 1]$). Even though $\operatorname{Ham}(P, W) = 1$ (only index $2$ differs), $\operatorname{prev}_P$ and $\operatorname{prev}_W$ differ at **two** indices ($j = 2$ and $j = 3$) because changing $W[2]$ from $\texttt{a}$ to $\texttt{b}$ also changes the predecessor of $W[3] = \texttt{a}$ from $2$ back to $1$! Updating the next occurrence $\operatorname{next}_W[j]$ after editing $W[j]$ resolves this completely.
- **Complexity**: $O(N \log N + N \cdot 2^k k \log M)$ (or $O(N k^2 \log M)$ via majority/bipartite matching on $\le 2k$ mismatch blocks).
::::

### Problem `CP-V-04` — Distinct Relative Trend Vocabulary

A financial analytics system records a sequence of $N$ daily prices $A[1..N]$ ($1 \le N \le 5 \times 10^4$, $1 \le A[i] \le 10^9$). Two contiguous subarrays $U[1..\ell]$ and $V[1..\ell]$ of equal length $\ell$ are said to exhibit the **same relative price trend** if for every pair of offsets $1 \le a, b \le \ell$:
$$U[a] \le U[b] \iff V[a] \le V[b].$$
Compute the total number of **distinct relative price trends** among all $\binom{N+1}{2}$ non-empty contiguous subarrays $A[l..r]$ ($1 \le l \le r \le N$).

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N \le 5 \times 10^4$, $1 \le A[i] \le 10^9$, Time Limit $2.5\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination (`Order-Preserving` vs. `Cartesian-Tree` vs. `Parameterized` in `Ch 20`)**:
  - Do **not** confuse relative price trend equivalence ($U[a] \le U[b] \iff V[a] \le V[b]$) with **Cartesian-Tree Equivalence (`Cartesian-KMP`)**: the arrays $U = [2, 1, 3]$ and $V = [3, 1, 2]$ share the exact same min-heap Cartesian tree (`1` at the root with leaf children at indices $1$ and $3$), yet $U[1] < U[3]$ while $V[1] > V[3]$!
  - Thus we cannot use the $O(1)$ monotonic-stack Parent-Distance code $\operatorname{PD}_A[x]$ of Cartesian-Tree matching. Instead, this problem asks for the number of distinct **order-isomorphic substrings** of $A[1..N]$, which requires constructing the **Order-Preserving Suffix Array (`Order-SA`)** and summing $(N - \operatorname{SA}[r] + 1) - \operatorname{ord\text{-}LCP}(\operatorname{SA}[r-1], \operatorname{SA}[r])$.
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
How do we compare two suffixes $A[i..N]$ and $A[j..N]$ under order-preserving equivalence and find their Longest Common Order-Isomorphic Prefix $\ell = \operatorname{ord\text{-}LCE}(i, j)$?
For any prefix length $m$, the relative order of $A[i..i+m-1]$ is uniquely determined by the sequence of **local rank pairs** $(\operatorname{less}_i(k), \operatorname{eq}_i(k))$ for $k = 0, \dots, m - 1$, where:
$$\operatorname{less}_i(k) = \#\bigl\{r \in [i, i + k - 1] : A[r] < A[i + k]\bigr\}, \qquad \operatorname{eq}_i(k) = \#\bigl\{r \in [i, i + k - 1] : A[r] = A[i + k]\bigr\}.$$
Equivalently, by **Kubica et al.'s Immediate-Neighbor Sufficiency (`Ch 20` §2.1 / Theorem 20.3)**, if $A[i..i+k-1] \cong_{\mathrm{ord}} A[j..j+k-1]$, then $A[i..i+k] \cong_{\mathrm{ord}} A[j..j+k]$ iff $A[j+k]$ satisfies the exact same `<` or `==` relation against the immediate predecessor witness $A[j + \operatorname{LMax}_i(k)]$ and successor witness $A[j + \operatorname{LMin}_i(k)]$ that $A[i+k]$ satisfies in $A[i..i+k-1]$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
We can compute $\operatorname{ord\text{-}LCE}(i, j)$ and sort all $N$ suffixes in $O(N \log^2 N)$ or $O(N \log^3 N)$ time using either of two persistent structures:

1. **Method A (Persistent Segment Tree of Polynomial Hashes via Single/Bounded Mutation)**:
   - Similar to Baker's `p-SA` (`Ch 20` §1.3 / Theorem 20.2), or using a **Persistent Wavelet Tree** over coordinate-compressed $A[1..N]$: for any candidate length $m$, or by walking the Wavelet Tree / maintaining dynamic predecessor links as $i$ steps from $N$ down to $1$, we can test whether $A[i..i+m-1] \cong_{\mathrm{ord}} A[j..j+m-1]$.
2. **Method B (Doubling / Prefix-Doubling Equivalence Classes on Local Ranks)**:
   - Even simpler to implement without dynamic tree splits: in prefix-doubling step $h = 0, 1, \dots, \lceil \log_2 N \rceil$, two substrings $A[i..i+2^h-1]$ and $A[j..j+2^h-1]$ are order-isomorphic iff they have the same order-isomorphism class at length $2^{h-1}$ **and** the merged sorted order of their left and right halves matches—or by maintaining a **Persistent Fenwick/Segment Tree** to query $(\operatorname{less}_i(k), \operatorname{eq}_i(k))$ in $O(\log N)$ time at the first mismatching offset!
3. Once all $N$ suffixes are sorted into $\operatorname{SA}[1..N]$ with adjacent common prefix lengths $\operatorname{ord\text{-}LCP}[r] = \operatorname{ord\text{-}LCE}(\operatorname{SA}[r-1], \operatorname{SA}[r])$, output:
   $$\sum_{r=1}^{N} \bigl(N - \operatorname{SA}[r] + 1 - \operatorname{ord\text{-}LCP}[r]\bigr).$$
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-V-04"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 20](../chapters/ch20-structural-isomorphism-weighted-strings.qmd) (`T-3B-04`: Order-Preserving Isomorphism, Immediate-Neighbor `LMax`/`LMin` Sufficiency & Order-Preserving Suffix Array; Generalized Matching Decoy · Part 3)**.
- **Why Tie-Breaking on Duplicate Values Requires Both $(\operatorname{less}, \operatorname{eq})$**:
  If $A$ contains duplicate prices, defining the local code solely by $\operatorname{less}_i(k) = \#\{r \in [i, i+k-1] : A[r] < A[i+k]\}$ fails to distinguish $U = [1, 2, 2]$ (where $\operatorname{less} = [0, 1, 1]$) from $V = [1, 3, 2]$ (where $\operatorname{less} = [0, 1, 1]$ as well!). Including the equality flag $\operatorname{eq}_i(k) > 0$ (or checking `LMax_eq[k]` against the predecessor witness) makes the local code a bijection with the weak-order equivalence class of $A[i..i+k]$.

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-5-05`)**:
  - **Using Cartesian Parent-Distance `PD[x]` for Order-Preserving Matching**: Fails on $[2, 1, 3]$ vs. $[3, 1, 2]$. Cartesian-Tree matching only checks the nearest smaller-or-equal ancestor on the left, whereas Order-Preserving matching requires both the largest element $\le A[x]$ (`LMax`) and the smallest element $\ge A[x]$ (`LMin`) inside the active window.
- **Complexity**: $O(N \log^2 N)$ time and $O(N \log N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-V-05` — Compressed Binary Composition Oracle

A high-frequency binary sensor stream $S \in \{\texttt{0}, \texttt{1}\}^N$ of huge total length $N \le 10^9$ is stored in compressed form as $R$ alternating maximal contiguous blocks ($1 \le R \le 5000$):
$$S = c_1^{\ell_1} c_2^{\ell_2} \dots c_R^{\ell_R}, \qquad c_k \in \{\texttt{0}, \texttt{1}\}, \quad c_k \ne c_{k+1}, \quad \sum_{k=1}^{R} \ell_k = N.$$
You are given $Q$ online queries ($1 \le Q \le 10^5$). Each query provides two non-negative integers $(z, o)$ with $1 \le z + o \le N$ and asks whether there exists at least one contiguous substring of $S$ of length $L = z + o$ that contains **exactly $z$ zeros and $o$ ones**. Output `YES` or `NO` for each query.

- **Constraints**: $1 \le R \le 5000$, $1 \le N = \sum \ell_k \le 10^9$, $1 \le Q \le 10^5$, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination (`Ch 20` RLE Parikh Envelope vs. `Ch 21` SLP Seam Matching)**:
  - Because $S$ is compressed to length $N \le 10^9$, it is tempting to treat $S$ as a grammar-compressed string (`Ch 21`). However, the query does **not** specify the order of `0`s and `1`s—it only asks for the **multiset (Parikh vector) $(z, o)$**!
  - Conversely, in standard uncompressed binary jumbled matching (`Ch 20` ladder problem `W3B-34`), we precompute the minimum and maximum `1`-counts $[m_L, M_L]$ for every window length $L \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ in $O(N)$ space. Here $N \le 10^9$ makes an $O(N)$-element array impossible, while the number of runs $R \le 5000$ is small!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
By the **Binary Parikh Interval Continuity Theorem (`Ch 20` §3.1 / Theorem 20.5 — Burcsi et al. 2010)**, for any fixed window length $L \in [1, N]$, sliding a window of length $L$ by one character changes its `1`-count by $S[i+L] - S[i] \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$. By the discrete Intermediate Value Theorem, the set of achievable `1`-counts of length $L$ is the **entire contiguous integer interval $[m_L, M_L]$**:
$$\exists\, \text{substring of } S \text{ with } (z, o) \iff m_{z+o} \le o \le M_{z+o}.$$
Now exploit the Run-Length Encoding $c_1^{\ell_1} \dots c_R^{\ell_R}$:

> **The RLE Extremal Boundary Alignment Lemma**:
> For any window length $L \in [1, N]$, the maximum `1`-count $M_L$ is always achieved by a window $[p, p + L - 1]$ where **at least one endpoint ($p$ or $p + L - 1$) coincides with a boundary between a `1`-run and a `0`-run** (or lies completely inside a single `1`-run)!
> Why? If neither $p$ nor $p + L - 1$ touches a run boundary, we can slide the window left or right without crossing any run boundary:
>
> - If $S[p]$ and $S[p + L]$ are equal, sliding preserves the `1`-count until an endpoint hits a run boundary;
> - If $S[p] = \texttt{0}$ and $S[p + L] = \texttt{1}$, sliding right strictly **increases** the `1`-count!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. Let $P_k = \sum_{r=1}^k \ell_r$ be the prefix lengths and $O_k = \sum_{r=1}^k \mathbf{1}[c_r = \texttt{1}] \ell_r$ be the prefix `1`-counts ($0 \le k \le R$).
2. Consider any pair of run indices $1 \le i \le j \le R$:
   - **Maximum Envelope $M_L$**: When the left endpoint of the window starts at the beginning of a `1`-run $i$ ($P_{i-1}$) and the right endpoint moves across run $j$ ($L \in [P_{j-1} - P_{i-1}, P_j - P_{i-1}]$):
     - If $c_j = \texttt{1}$, the `1`-count increases linearly with slope $+1$: $o(L) = (O_{j-1} - O_{i-1}) + \bigl(L - (P_{j-1} - P_{i-1})\bigr)$, i.e., the number of `0`s $z = L - o(L) = (P_{j-1} - P_{i-1}) - (O_{j-1} - O_{i-1})$ is **constant** across the entire segment!
     - If $c_j = \texttt{0}$, the `1`-count stays constant at $O_{j-1} - O_{i-1}$ while $L$ increases.
3. Even simpler in $(z, o)$ coordinates:
   - For a fixed number of zeros $z$, what is the **maximum** number of ones $M_{\mathrm{ones}}(z)$ that can accompany $z$ zeros in a substring? Any such substring contains some contiguous range of `0`-runs cleanly inside it plus partial `0`-runs at its two ends, and grabs **100% of the adjacent outer `1`-runs** on both sides!
   - Thus for every pair of `1`-runs $i \le j$, let $Z(i, j)$ be the total number of `0`s strictly between run $i$ and run $j$, and $O(i, j)$ be the total number of `1`s in $[i, j]$. Then for any $z$ obtained by taking $Z(i, j)$ plus at most $\ell_{i-1} + \ell_{j+1}$ boundary zeros, we can achieve all $O(i, j)$ ones!
   - Equivalently, collect the $O(R^2)$ upper-envelope breakpoints of $M_L$ (and lower-envelope breakpoints of $m_L$) in $O(R^2)$ time, sort/merge them into a monotone piecewise-linear envelope of $\le R^2$ segments with slopes in $\{0, 1\}$, and answer each query $(z, o)$ in **$O(\log R)$ time via binary search**!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-V-05"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 20](../chapters/ch20-structural-isomorphism-weighted-strings.qmd) (`T-3B-04`: Binary Parikh Interval Continuity & RLE Piecewise-Linear Extremal Envelopes)**.
- **Direct $(z, o)$ Step-Function Simplification ($O(R^2)$ Preprocessing, $O(\log R)$ Query)**:
  Because $m_{z+o} \le o \le M_{z+o}$ is equivalent to asking whether $(z, o)$ lies between the **maximum ones for $z$ zeros** ($\operatorname{MaxOne}(z)$) and **minimum ones for $z$ zeros** ($\operatorname{MinOne}(z)$):

  - To maximize `1`s for a given `0`-budget $z$: the optimal window always starts at the very left end of some `1`-run (or inside a `0`-run just before it) and ends at the very right end of some `1`-run (or inside the `0`-run just after it), so it never wastes a single available `1` at its boundaries! Specifically, for every pair of `1`-runs $i \le j$, let $z_{\mathrm{mid}}$ be the count of `0`s between them, $z_{\mathrm{ext}} = \ell_{i-1} + \ell_{j+1}$ be the adjacent `0`-runs, and $o_{\mathrm{tot}}$ be the sum of `1`s in $[i..j]$. This pair covers all $z \in [z_{\mathrm{mid}}, z_{\mathrm{mid}} + z_{\mathrm{ext}}]$ with up to $o_{\mathrm{tot}}$ ones! (Plus single runs: $z = 0$ achieves up to $\max_{c_i=\texttt{1}} \ell_i$ ones.)
  - Symmetrically, to maximize `0`s for a given `1`-budget $o$ (which is equivalent to minimizing `1`s for $z$), swap the roles of `0` and `1`!
  - Taking the prefix maximum of these $O(R^2)$ interval updates over coordinate-compressed breakpoints answers every query $(z, o)$ by checking $o \le \operatorname{MaxOne}(z)$ and $z \le \operatorname{MaxZero}(o)$ in $O(\log R)$ time!
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-5-06`)**:
  - **Applying Parikh Continuity to Ternary Alphabets $|\Sigma| \ge 3$**: Works **only** for $|\Sigma| = 2$ (where $z + o = L$ reduces a 2D vector to a 1D scalar). For $|\Sigma| = 3$, `S = abbc` at $L = 2$ has $(1,1,0), (0,2,0), (0,1,1)$ but skips $(1,0,1)$.
  - **Forgetting Windows Inside a Single Run ($z = 0$ or $o = 0$)**: Always initialize $\operatorname{MaxOne}(0) = \max_{c_i=\texttt{1}} \ell_i$ and $\operatorname{MaxZero}(0) = \max_{c_i=\texttt{0}} \ell_i$.
- **Complexity**: $O(R^2 \log R + Q \log R)$ time and $O(R^2)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-V-06` — Macro-to-Macro Substring Occurrence Census

In a symbolic verification engine, both a pattern string $P$ and a text string $T$ are generated by deterministic concatenation macro sequences:

- The pattern macro program has $V_P$ variables $P_1, \dots, P_{V_P}$ ($1 \le V_P \le 1500$), where each variable is either a single terminal letter $P_k = c \in \Sigma$ or a concatenation $P_k = P_{a_k} + P_{b_k}$ ($1 \le a_k, b_k < k$), and $P = P_{V_P}$.
- The text macro program has $V_T$ variables $T_1, \dots, T_{V_T}$ ($1 \le V_T \le 1500$) defined in the same manner, and $T = T_{V_T}$.

Both $|P|$ and $|T|$ can be as large as $10^{18}$. Compute the exact number of times the full string $P$ occurs as a contiguous substring of $T$, modulo $10^9 + 7$.

- **Constraints**: $1 \le V_P, V_T \le 1500$, $1 \le |P| \le |T| \le 10^{18}$, Time Limit $3.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $512\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination (`Ch 21` Primary-Seam KMP vs. Simultaneous Jeż Recompression)**:
  - In `Ch 21`'s Stepping-Stone SLP problem (`W3B-35`), the pattern $P$ is an *explicit* string of length $|P| \le 10^5$, so we can extract $\operatorname{suff}_{|P|-1}(X_L) + \operatorname{pref}_{|P|-1}(X_R)$ and run KMP in $O(V_T |P|)$ time.
  - **Why does that fail here?** Because here $|P|$ itself is up to $10^{18}$! You cannot unpack $P$ or slice length-$|P|$ seam windows. Even Border-AP seam compression (`O(V_T \log^2 |P| + |P|)`) fails to build the KMP automaton of $P$ if you try to unpack $P$.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Instead of unpacking $P$, apply **Jeż's Recompression (`RComp` + $\Sigma_L \times \Sigma_R$ `PComp`, `Ch 21` §1.3)** **simultaneously in lockstep** to the grammar rules of **both** $P$ and $T$ until $P$ shrinks to a single symbol of length $1$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Why would naively compressing $P$ and $T$ with `RComp` (replacing $c^\ell \to \langle c, \ell \rangle$) and `PComp` (replacing $ab \in \Sigma_L \times \Sigma_R \to d$) fail at the **boundaries** of $P$?
Suppose $P = \texttt{a}^2 \texttt{b} \texttt{c}^3$ occurs inside $T = \dots \texttt{a}^5 \texttt{b} \texttt{c}^4 \dots$.

- Inside $T$, `RComp` compresses the surrounding run of `a`s into $\langle \texttt{a}, 5 \rangle$, whereas at the left end of $P$, `RComp` sees only $\langle \texttt{a}, 2 \rangle$!
- Similarly, during `PComp` ($\Sigma_L \times \Sigma_R$), if $P$ starts with a symbol $P[0] \in \Sigma_R$, then inside $T$ that symbol $P[0]$ might pair with the preceding character $T[i-1] \in \Sigma_L$, whereas at the very front of $P$ there is no preceding character!

> **Jeż's Boundary-Popping Synchronization Invariant (2015)**:
> Before executing `RComp` or `PComp` at level $h$ on both $P$ and $T$:
>
> 1. **If $|P^{(h)}|$ is a single monochromatic run $a^m$**: Stop immediately! Every occurrence of $a^m$ in $T^{(h)}$ either lies inside a single terminal/run or crosses a seam $a^{\ell_1} \mid a^{\ell_2}$ in $T^{(h)}$ (contributing $\max(0, \min(\ell_1, m-1) + \min(\ell_2, m-1) - m + 1)$ occurrences).
> 2. **Before `RComp`**: Pop the maximal prefix run $a^{\ell_{\mathrm{pref}}}$ and maximal suffix run $b^{\ell_{\mathrm{suff}}}$ from $P^{(h)}$ (leaving $P'^{(h)}$), and replace every maximal run $a^{\ell}$ in $T^{(h)}$ ($\ell \ge \ell_{\mathrm{pref}}$ at right seam, etc.) by compound meta-symbols that expose the required prefix/suffix sub-runs, **or** simply note that an occurrence of $a^{\ell_{\mathrm{pref}}} P'^{(h)} b^{\ell_{\mathrm{suff}}}$ in $T^{(h)}$ matches $P'^{(h)}$ on interior blocks and requires the preceding RLE block in $T^{(h)}$ to be $\langle a, \ge \ell_{\mathrm{pref}} \rangle$ and the following RLE block to be $\langle b, \ge \ell_{\mathrm{suff}} \rangle$!
> 3. **Before `PComp` ($\Sigma_L \times \Sigma_R$)**: If $P^{(h)}$ starts with $r \in \Sigma_R$, pop $r$ from the front of $P^{(h)}$ and prepend $r$ to the right-hand side of wherever it is needed (or split $r$ out of its $\Sigma_L \times \Sigma_R$ pair in $P$); symmetrically, if $P^{(h)}$ ends with $\ell \in \Sigma_L$, pop $\ell$ from the back of $P^{(h)}$. Now **every** remaining symbol of $P^{(h)}$ starts in $\Sigma \setminus \Sigma_R$ and ends in $\Sigma \setminus \Sigma_L$, so $P^{(h)}$ cannot straddle any $\Sigma_L \times \Sigma_R$ pair boundary in $T^{(h)}$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. Represent each grammar variable $X_u \to X_L X_R$ in $P$ and $T$ alongside its explicit prefix/suffix character (or run) when needed.
2. Alternate **Phase A (`RComp`)** and **Phase B (`PComp`)**:
   - In **Phase A (`RComp`)**, for each rule $X_u \to X_L X_R$, if the last symbol of $X_L$ and first symbol of $X_R$ are runs of the same character $c$, pull them out of $X_L$ and $X_R$ and merge them at the seam of $X_u$ into $\langle c, \ell_1 + \ell_2 \rangle$.
   - In **Phase B (`PComp`)**, collect all bigrams $(x, y)$ appearing in rules of $P$ and $T$, greedily partition the active alphabet into $\Sigma_L \sqcup \Sigma_R$ so at least $1/2$ of adjacent positions in $P$ fall in $\Sigma_L \times \Sigma_R$, pop $P[0]$ (if $\in \Sigma_R$) and $P[\text{last}]$ (if $\in \Sigma_L$) from $P$, and contract all $(x, y) \in \Sigma_L \times \Sigma_R$ across the rules of $P$ and $T$ (pulling $X_L[\text{last}] \in \Sigma_L$ and $X_R[\text{first}] \in \Sigma_R$ across the seam of $X_u \to X_L X_R$!).
3. Because $|P|$ shrinks by a factor of $\le 3/4$ per phase, after $O(\log |P|) \le 130$ phases $P$ reduces to a single character or run, and we count its occurrences bottom-up on $T$ in $O((V_P + V_T) \log |P|)$ time!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-V-06"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 21](../chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd) (`T-3B-05`: Jeż's Recompression on Straight-Line Programs & Synchronized SLP-in-SLP Matching; Hierarchical Indexing Decoy · Part 1)**.
- **Why Pulling Seam Symbols Does Not Blow Up Grammar Size**:
  At each level $h$, a production rule $X_u \to X_L X_R$ absorbs at most $O(1)$ popped boundary symbols from $X_L$ and $X_R$ (and passes its own outer boundary symbols up to its parent). By converting the $O(1)$ intermediate symbols at the seam of $X_u$ back into $O(1)$ auxiliary binary rules (or storing a short explicit list of length $\le 4$ inside $X_u$), the number of active rules remains $O(V_P + V_T)$ at every single level!

- **Alternative via `Ch 21` Locally Consistent SLP-LCE + Border APs**:
  One can also build the $O(\log |P|)$-time deterministic SLP-LCE oracle (`Ch 21` §2.2) on the joint grammar of $P$ and $T$: using SLP-LCE, we can extract the $O(\log |P|)$ Border APs of $P$ and compute for each variable $T_u \to T_L T_R$ the $O(\log |P|)$ APs of prefixes of $P$ that are suffixes of $T_L$ (and suffixes of $P$ that are prefixes of $T_R$), intersecting them across the seam in $O((V_P + V_T) \log^3 |P|)$ time!

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-5-07`)**:
  - **Failing to Stop Pair Compression When $P = a^m$ Is Purely Unary**: A unary string $a^m$ has no $\Sigma_L \times \Sigma_R$ transitions ($a$ cannot be in both $\Sigma_L$ and $\Sigma_R$). Always check if $P$ has collapsed to a single run $\langle a, m \rangle$ at the start of `RComp`.
- **Complexity**: $O((V_P + V_T) \log |P|)$ time and $O(V_P + V_T)$ space via Jeż Recompression.
::::

### Problem `CP-V-07` — Dynamic Manuscript Editor & Pattern Census

You are maintaining a text manuscript $T$ of initial length $N \le 10^5$ under $Q \le 10^5$ online operations of two types:

1. **`CutPaste(l, r, pos)`**: Excise the contiguous substring $U = T[l..r]$ from $T$ (shrinking $T$ to $T[1..l-1] + T[r+1..|T|]$) and immediately re-insert $U$ right after index `pos` of the remaining string.
2. **`Count(P)`**: Given an explicit query pattern $P[1..M]$ ($\sum M \le 2 \times 10^5$), return the exact number of occurrences of $P$ as a contiguous substring of the current manuscript $T$.

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N, Q \le 10^5$, $\sum M \le 2 \times 10^5$, Time Limit $3.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $512\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination (`Ch 21` Locally Consistent Parsing vs. Static LZ77/Wavelet Indexing vs. Treap Hashing)**:
  - A static Suffix Automaton, Suffix Array, or LZ77 2D Wavelet Index (`Ch 21` §3.3 / Theorem 21.5) cannot survive arbitrary $O(\log N)$ substring `CutPaste` edits without expensive rebuilds.
  - Conversely, maintaining $T$ in a standard FHQ-Treap only supports $O(\log N)$ substring hashing, which would require $O(|P| \log N)$ per candidate alignment—still $\Theta(N)$ per `Count(P)` query unless the internal tree nodes of $T$ and $P$ **align deterministically regardless of global shift**!
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Maintain $T$ in a **Locally Consistent Parse Tree (`Ch 21` §1–§2)** of height $H = O(\log N)$ where block boundaries depend **only on a local neighborhood of radius $\Delta = O(1)$**. Then:
  - Each `CutPaste(l, r, pos)` is two `Split`s and two `Concat`s, modifying **at most $O(1)$ blocks per level** ($O(\log N)$ total time)!
  - Each `Count(P)` parses $P[1..M]$ using the **exact same local block compressor**, stripping $O(\Delta) = O(1)$ margin symbols from the left and right ends of $P^{(h)}$ at each level $h = 0, \dots, O(\log M)$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Let $T^{(0)}, T^{(1)}, \dots, T^{(H)}$ be the hierarchy of compressed sequences of $T$ produced by alternating `RComp` (maximal runs $c^\ell \to \langle c, \ell \rangle$) and `PComp` (`splitmix64` local-extrema cutting or Cole–Vishkin 6-coloring, lookahead radius $\Delta = O(1)$).

Now apply the **exact same level-$h$ parser** to the query pattern $P^{(h)}$:

> **The Margin-Stripping Interior Alignment Invariant (Alstrup–Brodal–Rauhe / Mehlhorn et al.)**:
> Because whether a block boundary is placed between $S^{(h)}[i-1]$ and $S^{(h)}[i]$ depends *only* on $S^{(h)}[i - \Delta .. i + \Delta]$, any occurrence of $P^{(h)}$ inside $T^{(h)}$ induces the **100% identical level-$(h+1)$ block sequence** on the interior of $P^{(h)}$ once we strip at most $\Delta + 1 = O(1)$ blocks from the left end and $\Delta + 1 = O(1)$ blocks from the right end of $P^{(h)}$!
>
> Explicitly, at each level $h$:
>
> 1. Any occurrence of $P^{(h)}$ in $T^{(h)}$ that is **short enough** to be spanned by a single parent block (or a pair of adjacent blocks at a seam when $|P^{(h)}| \le 2\Delta + 2$) is counted directly at level $h$ and recorded!
> 2. For longer occurrences ($|P^{(h)}| > 2\Delta + 2$), we strip the exact left margin $L^{(h)}$ and right margin $R^{(h)}$ at the first/last interior cut points of $P^{(h)}$, compress the interior into $P^{(h+1)}$, and promote the search to level $h + 1$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. **Dynamic Parse DAG Maintenance (`Split` & `Concat`)**:
   - Store the parse tree of $T$, where each level-$h$ node $u$ stores its symbol ID $\operatorname{id}(u)$, expanded length $\operatorname{len}(u)$, child list (size $\in [2, 4]$ for `PComp` or `(char, count)` for `RComp`), and the **active occurrence count** $\operatorname{cnt}[u]$ of symbol $\operatorname{id}(u)$ in the current tree $T$!
   - During `Split` and `Concat`, only $O(1)$ nodes per level are unpacked and re-compressed; decrement $\operatorname{cnt}[\text{old\_id}]$ when a block is unpacked and increment $\operatorname{cnt}[\text{new\_id}]$ when a new block is formed ($O(\log N)$ updates per `CutPaste`).
2. **Answering `Count(P)` in $O(|P| + \log^2 N)$ Time**:
   - Even simpler than tracking margin constraints across levels: since every occurrence of $P$ in $T$ crosses a **unique highest seam** $X_u \to X_{c_1} \dots X_{c_d}$ in the Locally Consistent Parse Tree (its **Primary Seam**, `Ch 21` §2.2 / Theorem 21.2!), how many distinct symbol types $X_u$ in the parse tree can have $P$ cross their primary seam *and* be the **minimal** node containing $P$?
   - By the Margin-Stripping Invariant, as we compress $P = P^{(0)} \to P^{(1)} \to \dots \to P^{(k)}$ until $|P^{(k)}| = O(1)$, at each level $h$ there are only **$O(1)$ canonical ways** that $P^{(h)}$ can straddle a seam of $T^{(h)}$ without being promoted to $P^{(h+1)}$!
   - Thus we compress $P$ bottom-up in $O(|P| + \log M)$ time; at each level $h$, we query the hash table of active level-$(h+1)$ block types $X_u$ whose child seam matches the stripped/unstripped core of $P^{(h)}$, summing $\operatorname{cnt}[X_u]$ in $O(1)$ time per level!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-V-07"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 21](../chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd) (`T-3B-05`: Locally Consistent Parsing, $O(1)$-Seam Split/Concat & Margin-Stripped Dynamic Pattern Matching; Hierarchical Indexing Decoy · Part 2)**.
- **Why Local Consistency Beats General SLPs for Online Pattern Queries**:
  In an *arbitrary* SLP of $g$ rules (`Ch 21` §2.2 / Theorem 21.2), a pattern $P$ can straddle the seam of **every single one** of the $g$ rules in a different way, forcing $O(g \cdot |P|)$ or $O(g \log^2 |P|)$ work per query. In a **Locally Consistent Parse Tree**, however, the parse of any substring $T[i..i+M-1] = P$ is **uniquely forced on its interior** by $P$ itself!
  Specifically, at level $h$, once $|P^{(h)}| \ge 2\Delta + 3$, the first interior cut point $l_h \in [1, \Delta+2]$ and last interior cut point $r_h \in [|P^{(h)}|-\Delta-1, |P^{(h)}|-1]$ of $P^{(h)}$ are 100% determined by $P^{(h)}$ alone (since their radius-$\Delta$ neighborhoods lie strictly inside $P^{(h)}$!). Therefore:

  - The interior $P^{(h)}[l_h .. r_h - 1]$ compresses deterministically into a **single unique sequence** $P_{\mathrm{int}}^{(h+1)}$.
  - At the single level $h^*$ where $P_{\mathrm{int}}^{(h^*+1)}$ first becomes empty (because $|P^{(h^*)}| \le 2\Delta + 2$), any occurrence of $P$ in $T$ is completely contained inside $\le 2$ adjacent blocks at level $h^* + 1$ (straddling the seam of a single block at level $h^* + 2$), which is looked up in $O(1)$ time per candidate margin extension!
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-5-08`)**:
  - **Omitting `RComp` Before Local-Extrema `PComp` Cuts**: On $P = \texttt{a}^M$ inside $T = \texttt{a}^N$, no strict local extrema exist; skipping `RComp` forces position-parity cuts that desynchronize shifts by $1$. Always execute `RComp` first at every level $h$ so $W[i] \ne W[i+1]$ everywhere.
- **Complexity**: $O(\log N)$ per `CutPaste` operation and $O(|P| + \log N)$ per `Count(P)` query.
::::

Map `'?'` $\mapsto (0,0)$ and $c \mapsto (1, \operatorname{ord}(c) \in [1..|\Sigma|])$ so $D_{\mathrm{ind}}(i) \le M(|\Sigma|-1)^2 < Q$. |
